When you think about how fast technology is moving, I think we’re imagining experiences today that can be had at the edge, that live within the compute constraints and the battery constraints that we have. Two years from now, those constraints are going to still be there, but the amount of capability you have will be larger. I think we’re going to continue to see innovation and invention in the space that’s going to create experiences we haven’t imagined yet.One of the things that I’m really curious about is just the amount of audio input all of these companies want to do. We had the CEO of Zoom on Decoder, and he was like, “Everyone will talk to AI avatars in Zoom and all of us will be mediated by Zoom. And that means we’ve got to record the in-person meeting. Everyone has to wear the rings or the pendants, and we’re going to record everything all day long so the AI can fully know us.” I have a lot of thoughts about that, but that’s one vision in the world. We’re going to record everything, which sort of puts a lot of pressure on noise cancellation, on rehabilitating the audio once you have it. There’s not just a lot of noise, but damage that happens in the compression process and transmitting over the internet. That all seems like an opportunity for a company like Bose.Is that where the investment is to help the AI hardware companies deal with lossy streaming and TikTok audio? What do you think about that opportunity?One of the things that we’re learning as we further venture into this space is that the core problems are the same. If you take something like speech clarity, voice pickup, that is a world we’ve done a lot of research on, a lot of work on. It’s an incredibly important part of a Bose headphone, for example, but it’s also important in a dozen other places where the same type of technology, at its core, can be expanded and extended.So think about driving 70 miles an hour down the highway in my car. That same speech clarity technology is really relevant in the car in the same way it is in a headphone, in the same way that it is in a motorcycle helmet, where you can imagine that’s maybe the most hostile sound environment you could get.I think the same is true. Noise-canceling has all sorts of varieties that, I think, are incredibly important in the AI examples that you talked about and in a lot of other everyday life examples where noise cancellation hasn’t gone yet. A great example of that is hearing aids. As you know, we’ve been working on hearing aid technology at Bose for over a decade. Just this year, we launched the world’s first hearing aid with a customer and partner called ORKA in China that has noise cancellation.It actually now solves what I think is the biggest problem that hearing aids have had for decades, which is that my most challenging environment, if I have some hearing loss, is a noisy restaurant, for example. And traditional hearing aids amplify all of that sound. Noise canceling has always been the dream of hearing aids because if you could take the noise of the environment down and amplify the speaker, the person you’re trying to have a conversation with, that’s sort of the holy grail now because you’re doing exactly what the customer really wants and needs.That, up until now, has been impossible to do because in a hearing aid, you need 15 to 18 hours of battery life. You have very limited compute. It’s been a really tricky problem. For us, solving that problem was both about hardware — a new driver that actually fits in the ear canal, but can power noise canceling — and the platform that we built to enable that at a low enough compute level that you could do it inside of a hearing aid over a period of 15 to 18 hours in a day. That’s the kind of innovation for noise canceling, for example, where it’s an obvious use case, but to get there required a considerable number of building blocks.I’m glad you brought up hearing aids. The last time you were on the show, you had a partnership, I believe, with Lexie. And after our conversation, I ran out and bought my dad those hearing aids. After four years, he won’t wear them because he says everything is too loud. Exactly the problem you’re describing.But you exited that partnership with Lexie, and the parent company — just asked a couple of weeks ago — is leaving the US market. They’re out. You’re describing hearing aids that you’re making in China. Is there something particular about the US market that just makes it too hard, or are you going to reenter?No, we’ve been here with Lexie, and they’re going through some challenges, and so we’ll find the right partner for us in the US. I think the over-the-counter hearing aid market has struggled more than any of us thought. If you go back four years, it hasn’t taken off at the rate we had hoped that it would. But I still see a ton of opportunity in the hearing aid space. And this hearing aid happens to be in China, but there’s no reason that you won’t see it in other places around the world.Why do you think it hasn’t taken off? I think it hasn’t worked yet. There are a couple of factors. And again, we’ve been partnering into it, so we’re not as close to the day-to-day. But I think there are really two things. It’s definitely cheaper and more accessible than it was in a prescription environment, but these are still very expensive products. So, rounding about a thousand dollars, which is a lot of money.I think in an over-the-counter space, most customers are expecting something that looks and feels more like what they would be willing to pay for a consumer electronics product, which is more like two, three, or maybe $400. While it’s more affordable, it is not as affordable as I think the consumer wants, needs, or expects. I still think there’s some work to do there from a technology standpoint to figure out how you bring it down.It’s also not really in the insurance space yet. If I get a prescription hearing aid that’s covered by Medicare or that’s covered by my insurance company, but that’s not the case for over-the-counter. And so I think there’s just some affordability challenges we haven’t quite fully solved yet — ones that the industry has not solved. That’s one piece of it. I also think there’s still a stigma part of it. There’s just still a, I don’t want to look old. I don’t want to feel old. I don’t want to wear a hearing aid. And until we figure out the right industrial design and make it more palatable, I think you still have resistance no matter the price point.The hearing aids my dad was most resistant to were when I tried to get him to wear AirPods, after Apple had released that feature. He looked at me and said, “Absolutely not.” So this is a particular area of convergence. What is an augmented reality hearing device except a hearing aid? Except a hearing aid with intense noise cancellation that can focus on the speaker in front of you and maybe translate them in real time if you don’t speak the same language? You’re talking to an AI, and you just want to whisper so no one can hear you, and it’s talking to you, but you’re still hearing everything that goes on. This is the convergence, right? The idea of headphones, the idea of augmented reality, and the idea of hearing aids, they’re in a Venn diagram. And the center of that Venn diagram, I think, is getting bigger and bigger over time.I just keep coming back to the same question: Is the culture of Bose designed to provide technology to all of the players in that ecosystem? Or are you still trying to win with the best product that hits the middle of that Venn diagram?We are always focused on who the Bose customer is and what the features they want are. As I’ve said a couple of times, you can’t fit everything in. That Venn diagram is getting bigger as compute is getting more powerful at the edge, but it’s still limited.When it comes to adding AI, we talk about it at Bose as tiny AI. A lot of companies are good at really big AI. What we’re good at is taking really complex algorithms and then figuring out how to shrink them down and take as little power and compute as they possibly can so that they can fit in our devices. But you’re always constrained. So we’re looking at what our customers are asking us for, what they need, what they want in that Venn diagram. Where do they want the emphasis to be? And that’s where we’re pushing our products. You’ll continue to see us do that.Other companies will choose a slightly different variation of that Venn diagram, and they’ll look for a different feature set. And I think that’s what makes the industry go. It is competitive by nature, and it is important to have a deep understanding of what the customer needs are.Do you think that there’s any pressure on Bose just from the product manufacturing side? There are tariffs, there’s a lot of focus on what gets made in China. We talked briefly about protectability and whether or not you even want to sell into Chinese companies or Chinese OEMs who might turn around and take your technology, which we have seen at scale with Apple, Tesla, and others. Is it worth it to be chasing hardware at this time?I think, since COVID, the supply chain has become a more exciting environment.[Laughs] Sure.So it’s been a series of things. I think our perspective back then was that we said, “Look, it’s clear we’re going to need to be more flexible and more agile in our supply chain.” That, I think, became clear. We’ve done a lot of work to get ourselves into a position where we expect curveballs now; we just don’t know what they’re going to be. And when they come, we’ve designed ourselves in a way that we can adjust quickly, and we think we’re flexible enough to handle it.The world needs hardware. As much as everyone is enamored with software and AI, and those are the things creating the magic, perhaps, on the hardware these days, you still need physical things. We are a physical world. You need physical things, and we are going to continue to make physical things and roll with the curveballs that come our way.Have you moved manufacturing, meaningfully, out of China?We have, yeah. So we’re diversified across Asia. We also have manufacturing in North America for some of our products as well.Have you moved anything, meaningfully, back into the United States?The only thing we have in the US is McIntosh. So all of our McIntosh products are built in Binghamton, New York.It’s funny, because those are the only products you have that also wouldn’t benefit from the price cut of not having tariffs. You need to keep those prices really high. Have you thought about moving anything back to the United States to avoid whatever tariffs and bring prices down?We’ll always look at it. It’s a fulsome economic equation of not just economics, but also expertise. Consumer electronics expertise from a manufacturing perspective moved to Asia a long time ago. And so it’s both a cost and an expertise question. We look at it, we talk about it. If it ever makes sense, we’ll do it. Right now, those things don’t play out for us.I feel like I have to ask you about Bluetooth one more time here at the end of our conversation. I’ve waited.It is the limiting factor of so many things you are doing. It’s the limiting factor of how you can connect to phones. It will almost certainly be the limiting factor of how all these AI devices work.The manufacturers have really put Bluetooth in a box. There is a wall around what it can do and what they will ever allow it to do on their platforms. And then there are their extensions. And this is across the board. I’m not even singling out one manufacturer. I used to always single out Apple, but now they’re all doing it. So it’s like, great, there’s a wall around Bluetooth.For a company like Bose, which has to connect to phones, that is the limit. Have you tried to push hard to overcome that limit? Have the antics of the European Union helped you open up and overcome the limit? How has this played out over the last four years?Probably not terribly different from what we talked about last time. We partner, we push, we ask for what we want, and we work with what we have. So I think we are always trying to test and push the limits as much as we can, and we’re incredibly good at not using that as an excuse. So how do we create amazing experiences with the advantages that we have? And we think we’re pretty great at doing that.On the other side of this, you’ve got McIntosh products, your premium home products, and people are disconnected. A lot of people still want to play Spotify off their phone onto their home stereo system. There’s a joke we tell in our other show, the Vergecast, where we just try to locate the computer. Where is the computer supposed to be here?If you’re playing music off your phone, is the computer your phone, and you’re just Bluetooth streaming to your speakers? In the context of McIntosh, that is just like a heartbreaking crime. Don’t stream Bluetooth to your McIntosh system. So that means the McIntosh system needs a computer. It needs to run some variant of a Spotify app that has Wi-Fi that pulls lossless [audio] down. That means it needs a ramp. The whole thing immediately becomes a computer. Maybe a somewhat low-powered computer that’s only focused on a handful of apps, but a computer.You also have all the carrying costs of a computer. Software updates, application updates, Spotify changes its file formats. Whatever is going to happen, you’ve got some problem there. How do you think about that?Across all of your products, the amount of compute going into them is going up, as you’ve described. Maybe in tiny ways, but it’s going up. And then you’re not charging service fees. How does that all work as more and more of your products fundamentally become network computers?I think consumers are subscription’d out. I think that the idea that you’re going to create a subscription service over an over-the-air update that they’re going to pay for on a monthly basis, I think that’s not coming in our space. So we have to kind of think long term as we’re selling products today: what is the software, compute, cloud storage, all of the security, all of the costs that live across the life cycle of that product that we’re going to have to support. We have to build that into the cost of maintaining that product, right? Which is different from what you would have done in the past.We’ve made some design choices, I think, that are important as well. We don’t need to duplicate what Spotify is doing either. So as we think about the lifestyle collection products that we just launched, what we heard overwhelmingly from our customers was, “I just want to go to my music. I don’t understand why I have to deal with you. I love how this sounds, but please just get me to my music faster.” We thought for a long time about how best to do that in the home. And we think about it in our wearables too. We want you to be able to control your home speakers through Spotify, AirPlay, or however you want to do that. And that offloads some of that from Bose, which is good.We also just made an acquisition of a company called Stream Unlimited. Their business is to connect to all of the streaming apps, devices, et cetera, that allow a smart home device to have those easy connections. That gives us some scalability and some participation in that orchestration layer, which is also helpful for us. So we come at the problem in a couple of different ways.There are rumors, in a few months or weeks here, that Apple will put out a whole bunch of new smart home devices. OpenAI might put out a smart home device. Obviously, I have Google ones, and there are Amazon ones. You ask any of those companies, what are the number one and two things people ask for from their assistants in their house? And it’s setting timers and playing music. Then everything else is a long tail of almost nothing. The drop-off is enormous.If you want to play music and you’ve got a great stereo in your house, you’ve got to go connect to their smart home system. Now you’re on their network, and now you’re just another endpoint for whatever forthcoming successful consumer AI agent will exist. Big question mark there, but let’s say it happens.That further commodifies you, right? That’s yet another time when they’re not going to use your interface or your streaming; they’re just going to say [a command] out loud in their home, and the OpenAI device will be like, “I found some speakers on your network. I’m playing the music for you.” Do you need to participate there? Do you need the OpenAI agent to say, “I’m playing it on your Bose speakers,” and then you collect a tiny little licensing check back, or how should that work?I don’t think so. I think we understand there are a lot of components in this chain, and customers think about Bose for amazing sound. And when they’re playing the speaker, and they’re asking whatever agent they’re asking to play it, there is an appreciation. There is going to be a logo on that speaker. If you have a new Bose Lifestyle speaker, there’s going to be a logo right on the front of it. You’re going to look at it every day in your kitchen, living room, or wherever it’s placed.I get the feeling those logos are about to get bigger and start lighting up. You can see it coming.[Laughs] We’re not going to make them that big.So that chain is long. And in fact, you launched another piece of the chain of music, which is that you launched Studios, which feels like a record label, a marketing venture for new artists. How does that play into it?So bigger than a record label, not just a record label, but that’s a piece of it. Think about Bose Studios as a way to connect with our customers and give them new avenues to participate with us. The announcement may feel like a sudden thing, but if you sort of look at what we’ve been doing at Bose over the last four or five years, we’ve been moving in this direction.Getting the attention of consumers is hard. You don’t do that with traditional advertising anymore. Consumers are engaging with content, and that’s it. And so we’ve been building more and more content. We’ve been partnering with more and more creators. We’ve been dipping our toe in this water for the last several years.So I’ll give you a couple of examples. We’ve been partnering with NME to do their mixtape, where we’re helping them bring undiscovered, up-and-coming artists to the forefront and helping bring and celebrate those artists. We’ve learned a lot from doing that. The connection and the participation of our customers with that content and with those artists has been incredible.We’ve been sponsoring an event, the Chris Brickley Invitational, which is this amazing basketball event for high school basketball players. It is becoming the place to go if you’re an All-American type high school basketball player, both on the men’s and the women’s side. And that event has turned into something so special. We’re not putting on a new Super Bowl over here, but we are participating in content creation in a way that connects with our customers. We think that’s really important.We also like this idea of up-and-coming creators who need support to launch their careers. At Bose, we say fiercely independent. There’s something so unique about our structure and the independence that we have. We kind of like the idea of supporting this up-and-coming group. It supports our connection with our customers, and we think we’re helping them along the way as well.I feel like I could spend another full hour just talking about the economics of the music business and brands supporting creators in this way. But sadly, you’ve already given us too much time. Lila, thank you so much for being on Decoder.Thank you for having me back.Questions or comments? Hit us up at decoder@theverge.com. We really do read every email!Decoder with Nilay PatelA podcast from The Verge about big ideas and other problems.SUBSCRIBE NOW!Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.Nilay Patel

But I would say two things fundamentally have changed as we’ve thought about growth for Bose for the future.

blocks.html_en: For 60 years, it was all Bose, and we’re now a multi-brand company. So as you said, we’ve made a couple of acquisitions. sentences.zh: 当我们真正坐下来思考这个问题时，考虑到音乐是人们的热情所在，这对我们来说没有意义。

blocks.html_en: We think there’s a huge opportunity to attract new customers to the category if the experience feels more like a luxury experience. And so when you think about those products, it’s certainly about how they sound, but you went right to it. It’s the iconic design, it’s the artistry, it’s the craftsmanship. All of our luxury products, whether it’s McIntosh or Sonus faber, are handmade. They are crafted one by one for you as the customer. And there’s something incredibly special about that.

sentences.en: We think there’s a huge opportunity to attract new customers to the category if the experience feels more like a luxury experience.
sentences.zh: 我们认为，如果体验更像是一种奢华体验，那么就有巨大的机会吸引新客户进入该类别。

sentences.en: And so when you think about those products, it’s certainly about how they sound, but you went right to it.
sentences.zh: 因此，当您考虑这些产品时，肯定会考虑它们的声音，但您直接选择了它。

sentences.en: It’s the iconic design, it’s the artistry, it’s the craftsmanship.
sentences.zh: 这是标志性的设计，这是艺术性，这是工艺。

sentences.en: All of our luxury products, whether it’s McIntosh or Sonus faber, are handmade.
sentences.zh: 我们所有的奢侈品，无论是 McIntosh 还是 Sonus faber，都是手工制作的。

sentences.en: They are crafted one by one for you as the customer.
sentences.zh: 它们是为作为客户的您一一制作的。

sentences.en: And there’s something incredibly special about that.
sentences.zh: 这有一些非常特别的地方。

blocks.html_en: These weren’t your decisions, so I feel like I can be a little bit rude about them. When I saw McIntosh was licensing to Stellantis to be in Jeeps, I thought, “This company has to be desperate for money. That’s not actually a match.” It was fun that I had a Jeep with blue meters in it. It was great.

sentences.en: These weren’t your decisions, so I feel like I can be a little bit rude about them.
sentences.zh: 这些不是你的决定，所以我觉得我可能对它们有点粗鲁。

sentences.en: When I saw McIntosh was licensing to Stellantis to be in Jeeps, I thought, “This company has to be desperate for money.
sentences.zh: 当我看到 McIntosh 向 Stellantis 授权使用吉普车时，我想：“这家公司一定非常缺钱。

sentences.en: That’s not actually a match.”
sentences.zh: 这实际上不是一场比赛。”

sentences.en: It was fun that I had a Jeep with blue meters in it.
sentences.zh: 很有趣的是我有一辆装有蓝色仪表的吉普车。

sentences.en: It was great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

blocks.html_en: But I thought to myself, “This is a total mismatch, and they should be in Maybachs,” or whatever it is, whatever luxury sector that you want to be in, because that’s the brand. Was this just opportunistic for you that this was a company that needed the help, that was in trouble, that you could go and you could push your products upmarket without having to take the Bose brand there? Or was there some other opportunity that presented itself to you?

sentences.en: But I thought to myself, “This is a total mismatch, and they should be in Maybachs,” or whatever it is, whatever luxury sector that you want to be in, because that’s the brand.
sentences.zh: 但我心想，“这完全不匹配，他们应该是迈巴赫”，或者无论它是什么，无论你想进入哪个奢侈品领域，因为这就是品牌。

sentences.en: Was this just opportunistic for you that this was a company that needed the help, that was in trouble, that you could go and you could push your products upmarket without having to take the Bose brand there?
sentences.zh: 这对你来说只是机会主义吗？这是一家需要帮助、陷入困境的公司，你可以离开，你可以将你的产品推向高端市场，而不必将 Bose 品牌带到那里？

sentences.en: Or was there some other opportunity that presented itself to you?
sentences.zh: 或者还有其他机会出现在您面前吗？

blocks.html_en: We weren’t actually shopping for brands first. The first thing was, strategically, we saw the opportunity in the luxury space. We saw an opportunity to create something new around luxury audio, and we were really excited about that.

sentences.en: We weren’t actually shopping for brands first.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上并不是首先购买品牌。

sentences.en: The first thing was, strategically, we saw the opportunity in the luxury space.
sentences.zh: 首先，从战略上讲，我们看到了奢侈品领域的机会。

sentences.en: We saw an opportunity to create something new around luxury audio, and we were really excited about that.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了围绕豪华音频创造新事物的机会，我们对此感到非常兴奋。

blocks.html_en: So once we had made the strategic decision to go there, we had a lot of conversations about buying a brand or creating a brand. But the reality is, in luxury, at those price points, history and heritage are part of what you’re buying. And so we sort of intuitively knew we wanted to find a brand or brands that really had that strong history that we felt like we could build on top of.

sentences.en: So once we had made the strategic decision to go there, we had a lot of conversations about buying a brand or creating a brand.
sentences.zh: 因此，一旦我们做出了前往那里的战略决策，我们就购买品牌或创建品牌进行了很多对话。

sentences.en: But the reality is, in luxury, at those price points, history and heritage are part of what you’re buying.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，在奢侈品中，在这些价位上，历史和传统是你所购买的东西的一部分。

sentences.en: And so we sort of intuitively knew we wanted to find a brand or brands that really had that strong history that we felt like we could build on top of.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们直觉地知道我们想要找到一个或多个真正拥有悠久历史的品牌，我们觉得我们可以在此基础上继续发展。

blocks.html_en: We thought those were both brands that had incredibly passionate fans, and we saw an opportunity for us to take them to a new level. So that was how we ended up acquiring the McIntosh group.

sentences.en: We thought those were both brands that had incredibly passionate fans, and we saw an opportunity for us to take them to a new level.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这两个品牌都拥有非常热情的粉丝，我们看到了将它们提升到新水平的机会。

sentences.en: So that was how we ended up acquiring the McIntosh group.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们最终收购麦金托什集团的方式。

blocks.html_en: Bringing in their engineering organization, they have a lot of technology. How integrated has that become over time, or are you leaving them alone?

sentences.en: Bringing in their engineering organization, they have a lot of technology.
sentences.zh: 引入他们的工程组织，他们拥有很多技术。

sentences.en: How integrated has that become over time, or are you leaving them alone?
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，它们的整合程度如何，或者您是否对它们置之不理？

blocks.html_en: We’ve brought it into our engineering organization, but we’ve also kept a lot of the aspects a little bit separate. So probably the best example of that is Bose has a Bose sound. Everybody knows that. You buy a Bose product… You buy one, the headphones I’m wearing, the speaker in your house, your car. There is a sound signature to brands that consumers expect. That comes from the engineers.

sentences.en: We’ve brought it into our engineering organization, but we’ve also kept a lot of the aspects a little bit separate.
sentences.zh: 我们已将其纳入我们的工程组织中，但我们也将许多方面分开。

sentences.en: So probably the best example of that is Bose has a Bose sound.
sentences.zh: 最好的例子可能就是 Bose 的 Bose 声音。

sentences.en: Everybody knows that.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道这一点。

sentences.en: You buy a Bose product…
sentences.zh: 您购买 Bose 产品...

sentences.en: You buy one, the headphones I’m wearing, the speaker in your house, your car.
sentences.zh: 你买一个，我戴的耳机，你家里的扬声器，你的车。

sentences.en: There is a sound signature to brands that consumers expect.
sentences.zh: 消费者期望的品牌有一个良好的标志。

sentences.en: That comes from the engineers.
sentences.zh: 这来自工程师。

blocks.html_en: The engineers are tuning products to sound like they should. And so we’re very careful on the engineering side to protect the sound signature of McIntosh. What we don’t want is for you to hear a McIntosh product or a Sonus faber product and imagine that it sounds different. So that’s one.

sentences.en: The engineers are tuning products to sound like they should.
sentences.zh: 工程师们正在调整产品，使其听起来像他们应该的那样。

sentences.en: And so we’re very careful on the engineering side to protect the sound signature of McIntosh.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在工程方面非常小心，以保护麦金托什的声音特征。

sentences.en: What we don’t want is for you to hear a McIntosh product or a Sonus faber product and imagine that it sounds different.
sentences.zh: 我们不希望您听到 McIntosh 产品或 Sonus faber 产品并想象它听起来不同。

sentences.en: So that’s one.
sentences.zh: 这就是其中之一。

blocks.html_en: Initially — as you do with, I think, any acquisition — you want to be careful to protect what you bought. We’ve integrated it, yes, but we have a separate team that is doing the engineering for luxury, and we’re slowly adding Bose technology to it where it makes sense. So there are things, for example, on the Bose side where we can be incredibly helpful in terms of the software aspects, the connectivity, those sorts of things. Those are things that we do really well, and they’re not the most important part of those products, but they have to work. There are aspects that we’ve started to add into the products, and you’ll see more of that over time.

sentences.en: Initially — as you do with, I think, any acquisition — you want to be careful to protect what you bought.
sentences.zh: 最初——我认为，就像你对任何收购所做的那样——你要小心保护你所购买的东西。

sentences.en: We’ve integrated it, yes, but we have a separate team that is doing the engineering for luxury, and we’re slowly adding Bose technology to it where it makes sense.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们已经集成了它，但我们有一个单独的团队负责奢侈品工程，并且我们正在慢慢地将 Bose 技术添加到有意义的地方。

sentences.en: So there are things, for example, on the Bose side where we can be incredibly helpful in terms of the software aspects, the connectivity, those sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 例如，在 Bose 方面，我们可以在软件方面、连接性等方面提供令人难以置信的帮助。

sentences.en: Those are things that we do really well, and they’re not the most important part of those products, but they have to work.
sentences.zh: 这些是我们做得非常好的事情，它们不是这些产品中最重要的部分，但它们必须起作用。

sentences.en: There are aspects that we’ve started to add into the products, and you’ll see more of that over time.
sentences.zh: 我们已经开始在产品中添加一些功能，随着时间的推移，您会看到更多。

blocks.html_en: I’m really curious about that luxury aspect. The knock on high-end audio for years, and I’m not saying this is McIntosh, but the knock on high-end audio for years is that it’s the same stuff, all dressed up fancy. There are headphones that are famous for having weights in them to feel heavier even though there are commodity parts inside.

sentences.en: I’m really curious about that luxury aspect.
sentences.zh: 我对奢华方面真的很好奇。

sentences.en: The knock on high-end audio for years, and I’m not saying this is McIntosh, but the knock on high-end audio for years is that it’s the same stuff, all dressed up fancy.
sentences.zh: 多年来人们对高端音频的批评，我并不是说这是麦金托什，但多年来对高端音频的批评是，它们都是同样的东西，都装扮得很花哨。

sentences.en: There are headphones that are famous for having weights in them to feel heavier even though there are commodity parts inside.
sentences.zh: 有些耳机以带有重量而闻名，尽管里面有商品部件，但感觉更重。

blocks.html_en: This is one of those places where you could just say, “We’re just going to make more expensive versions of the same thing.” And some buyers are totally price-insensitive, in that they will always just buy the most expensive thing. Then there’s, “We’re going to make it worth it. We’re going to make it worth 10X the price of whatever Bluetooth speakers are at Best Buy.”

sentences.en: This is one of those places where you could just say, “We’re just going to make more expensive versions of the same thing.”
sentences.zh: 这是你可以说的地方之一，“我们只是要制作同一件事的更昂贵的版本。”

sentences.en: And some buyers are totally price-insensitive, in that they will always just buy the most expensive thing.
sentences.zh: 有些买家对价格完全不敏感，他们总是只买最贵的东西。

sentences.en: Then there’s, “We’re going to make it worth it.
sentences.zh: 然后是，“我们会让这一切变得值得。

sentences.en: We’re going to make it worth 10X the price of whatever Bluetooth speakers are at Best Buy.”
sentences.zh: 我们将使其价值是百思买蓝牙扬声器价格的 10 倍。”

blocks.html_en: Where are you falling on that? Because it’s very tempting, especially in luxury, to just make it expensive.

sentences.en: Where are you falling on that?
sentences.zh: 你在哪里？

sentences.en: Because it’s very tempting, especially in luxury, to just make it expensive.
sentences.zh: 因为让它变得昂贵是非常诱人的，尤其是在奢侈品领域。

blocks.html_en: The value comes from the sound. You should come visit us at Bose in Framingham and listen to a McIntosh system, a Sonus faber system. They’re incredible. They’re not anything like what you would get at a Best Buy in a premium product from Bose or anyone else. And that’s incredibly special.

sentences.en: The value comes from the sound.
sentences.zh: 价值来自于声音。

sentences.en: You should come visit us at Bose in Framingham and listen to a McIntosh system, a Sonus faber system.
sentences.zh: 您应该来弗雷明汉的 Bose 拜访我们，聆听 McIntosh 系统、Sonus faber 系统。

sentences.en: They’re incredible.
sentences.zh: 他们太不可思议了。

sentences.en: They’re not anything like what you would get at a Best Buy in a premium product from Bose or anyone else.
sentences.zh: 它们与您在百思买 (Best Buy) 购买的 Bose 或其他任何品牌的优质产品完全不同。

sentences.en: And that’s incredibly special.
sentences.zh: 这非常特别。

blocks.html_en: Part of that is the technology itself. Part of that is that it’s more analog, so it has a different sound signature to it. It’s got a lot more power behind it because that’s what McIntosh is known for, and that’s what you need to power a Sonus faber set of speakers. You’re also paying for design. In a way, it’s a little bit of art.

sentences.en: Part of that is the technology itself.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分是技术本身。

sentences.en: Part of that is that it’s more analog, so it has a different sound signature to it.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是它更加模拟，因此具有不同的声音特征。

sentences.en: It’s got a lot more power behind it because that’s what McIntosh is known for, and that’s what you need to power a Sonus faber set of speakers.
sentences.zh: 它背后有更多的动力，因为这就是 McIntosh 闻名的原因，也是您为 Sonus faber 扬声器组提供动力所需的动力。

sentences.en: You’re also paying for design.
sentences.zh: 您还为设计付费。

sentences.en: In a way, it’s a little bit of art.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这有点艺术。

blocks.html_en: We just launched a new integrated amplifier, the MA2375, for McIntosh. I’m so excited about it. It’s sort of got that retro look with the vacuum tubes. It is a design piece. I want to sit it on my desk. I want it to be a part of the decor. You would say the same thing on the Sonus faber side. It’s like buying an incredible piece of Italian furniture that has been handmade with natural materials and just feels like art that also sounds beautiful.

sentences.en: We just launched a new integrated amplifier, the MA2375, for McIntosh.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚为 McIntosh 推出了一款新的集成放大器 MA2375。

sentences.en: I’m so excited about it.
sentences.zh: 我对此感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: It’s sort of got that retro look with the vacuum tubes.
sentences.zh: 它的真空管有点复古的外观。

sentences.en: It is a design piece.
sentences.zh: 这是一件设计作品。

sentences.en: I want to sit it on my desk.
sentences.zh: 我想把它放在我的桌子上。

sentences.en: I want it to be a part of the decor.
sentences.zh: 我希望它成为装饰的一部分。

sentences.en: You would say the same thing on the Sonus faber side.
sentences.zh: 在 Sonus faber 方面你也会说同样的话。

sentences.en: It’s like buying an incredible piece of Italian furniture that has been handmade with natural materials and just feels like art that also sounds beautiful.
sentences.zh: 这就像购买一件令人难以置信的意大利家具，它是用天然材料手工制作的，感觉就像艺术品，听起来也很漂亮。

blocks.html_en: So there’s more to the value proposition in the luxury space. It’s true in the premium space too. Design really matters, color matters, feel, touch, comfort, all those things matter in addition to the sound. I think it’s just even that much more elevated in the luxury space.

sentences.en: So there’s more to the value proposition in the luxury space.
sentences.zh: 因此，奢侈品领域的价值主张还有更多。

sentences.en: It’s true in the premium space too.
sentences.zh: 在高端领域也是如此。

sentences.en: Design really matters, color matters, feel, touch, comfort, all those things matter in addition to the sound.
sentences.zh: 设计真的很重要，颜色很重要，感觉、触感、舒适度，除了声音之外，所有这些都很重要。

sentences.en: I think it’s just even that much more elevated in the luxury space.
sentences.zh: 我认为在奢侈品领域它的地位更高。

blocks.html_en: I’m really curious about all the different sets of new customers you’re describing. There’s the B2B business, which is growing in audio tech. Then there are luxury customers who have a lot of money, but they’re fickle. And particularly in high-end AV — and I’m a high-end AV nerd through and through — convincing people it’s worth it because they can hear it has always been the hardest problem.

sentences.en: I’m really curious about all the different sets of new customers you’re describing.
sentences.zh: 我真的对你所描述的所有不同的新客户群体感到好奇。

sentences.en: There’s the B2B business, which is growing in audio tech.
sentences.zh: B2B 业务在音频技术领域不断发展。

sentences.en: Then there are luxury customers who have a lot of money, but they’re fickle.
sentences.zh: 还有一些奢侈品客户虽然有很多钱，但变化无常。

sentences.en: And particularly in high-end AV — and I’m a high-end AV nerd through and through — convincing people it’s worth it because they can hear it has always been the hardest problem.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在高端 AV 领域——我是一个彻头彻尾的高端 AV 书呆子——让人们相信这是值得的，因为他们能听到它一直是最难的问题。

blocks.html_en: Maybe the most fun problem, because you can convince a lot of people they’re hearing a lot of things that aren’t there. You can sell expensive cables at a hundred times the price of the regular cables, even if they don’t do anything different. This is a lot of new customers for Bose. Do you think the B2B business is going to distract your core technology roadmap? How are you holding that all together?

sentences.en: Maybe the most fun problem, because you can convince a lot of people they’re hearing a lot of things that aren’t there.
sentences.zh: 也许是最有趣的问题，因为你可以让很多人相信他们听到了很多不存在的事情。

sentences.en: You can sell expensive cables at a hundred times the price of the regular cables, even if they don’t do anything different.
sentences.zh: 您可以以普通电缆一百倍价格出售昂贵的电缆，即使它们没有任何不同。

sentences.en: This is a lot of new customers for Bose.
sentences.zh: 这为 Bose 带来了很多新客户。

sentences.en: Do you think the B2B business is going to distract your core technology roadmap?
sentences.zh: 您认为 B2B 业务会分散您的核心技术路线图吗？

sentences.en: How are you holding that all together?
sentences.zh: 你是如何把这一切结合在一起的？

blocks.html_en: It is more complex for sure. It is a broader mission, and I think we’re ready for it. When I was here last time, we were in the middle of the transformation that I would say was solidifying the foundation of Bose, and now we’re building on top of that. We’ve built an amazing marketing and brand infrastructure that we’re now using to power three brands instead of one, but a lot of that capability can be put in the direction of all three.

sentences.en: It is more complex for sure.
sentences.zh: 它肯定更复杂。

sentences.en: It is a broader mission, and I think we’re ready for it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个更广泛的使命，我认为我们已经做好了准备。

sentences.en: When I was here last time, we were in the middle of the transformation that I would say was solidifying the foundation of Bose, and now we’re building on top of that.
sentences.zh: 当我上次来这里时，我们正处于转型之中，我想说的是，这正在巩固 Bose 的基础，而现在我们正在在此基础上继续发展。

sentences.en: We’ve built an amazing marketing and brand infrastructure that we’re now using to power three brands instead of one, but a lot of that capability can be put in the direction of all three.
sentences.zh: 我们已经建立了一个令人惊叹的营销和品牌基础设施，现在我们用它来为三个品牌而不是一个品牌提供动力，但其中很多能力都可以用于这三个品牌。

blocks.html_en: So the key is real clarity about who the customer is, which we’ve done a lot of work on the Bose brand for sure. We talk about the music lover for Bose, but we’ve done the same work for McIntosh and the same work for Sonus faber so that we are one thousand percent clear about who the customer is and how we want to talk to that customer.

sentences.en: So the key is real clarity about who the customer is, which we’ve done a lot of work on the Bose brand for sure.
sentences.zh: 因此，关键是要真正清楚地了解客户是谁，我们在 Bose 品牌上确实做了很多工作。

sentences.en: We talk about the music lover for Bose, but we’ve done the same work for McIntosh and the same work for Sonus faber so that we are one thousand percent clear about who the customer is and how we want to talk to that customer.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是 Bose 的音乐爱好者，但我们也为 McIntosh 和 Sonus faber 做了同样的工作，这样我们就 1000% 清楚客户是谁以及我们想如何与该客户交谈。

blocks.html_en: On the kind of products side of our company, I think we’re really clear about what the mission is for each one of those brands. On the technology side, interestingly, as we become more of a B2B technology company, it’s actually creating advantages back to the Bose brand and our luxury business as well. And what I mean by that is that it’s caused us to completely rethink the way that we do research and we develop our tech.

sentences.en: On the kind of products side of our company, I think we’re really clear about what the mission is for each one of those brands.
sentences.zh: 在我们公司的产品种类方面，我认为我们非常清楚每个品牌的使命是什么。

sentences.en: On the technology side, interestingly, as we become more of a B2B technology company, it’s actually creating advantages back to the Bose brand and our luxury business as well.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，在技术方面，随着我们越来越成为一家 B2B 技术公司，它实际上为 Bose 品牌和我们的奢侈品业务创造了优势。

sentences.en: And what I mean by that is that it’s caused us to completely rethink the way that we do research and we develop our tech.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它让我们彻底重新思考我们研究和开发技术的方式。

blocks.html_en: In the past, if you think about Bose developing products, we were developing purpose-built technology for a pair of headphones or a car audio system. And I think last time we talked about the tech franchises. We care a lot about noise cancellation. We care about immersive, lifelike audio, and we care about this idea of hearing what you want. And those are all experiences that are built on some basic building blocks of technology that we’ve been developing for a long time.

sentences.en: In the past, if you think about Bose developing products, we were developing purpose-built technology for a pair of headphones or a car audio system.
sentences.zh: 过去，如果您考虑 Bose 开发的产品，我们正在为耳机或汽车音响系统开发专用技术。

sentences.en: And I think last time we talked about the tech franchises.
sentences.zh: 我想上次我们讨论了科技特许经营权。

sentences.en: We care a lot about noise cancellation.
sentences.zh: 我们非常关心噪音消除。

sentences.en: We care about immersive, lifelike audio, and we care about this idea of hearing what you want.
sentences.zh: 我们关心身临其境、栩栩如生的音频，我们关心听到您想要的声音的想法。

sentences.en: And those are all experiences that are built on some basic building blocks of technology that we’ve been developing for a long time.
sentences.zh: 这些体验都是建立在我们长期以来开发的一些基本技术构建模块之上的。

blocks.html_en: But because we were developing them for our own products, we’ve had to do a complete shift in the way that we think about it so that we’re now developing, from the ground up, those building blocks. Now we’re able to say, with common platforms, common algorithms, AI — think of them as sort of AI units — we can create different experiences for our own products, and we can port that same technology through the same platform tech into other people’s products.

sentences.en: But because we were developing them for our own products, we’ve had to do a complete shift in the way that we think about it so that we’re now developing, from the ground up, those building blocks.
sentences.zh: 但因为我们是为自己的产品开发它们，所以我们必须彻底改变我们的思维方式，以便我们现在从头开始开发这些构建块。

sentences.en: Now we’re able to say, with common platforms, common algorithms, AI — think of them as sort of AI units — we can create different experiences for our own products, and we can port that same technology through the same platform tech into other people’s products.
sentences.zh: 现在我们可以说，通过通用平台、通用算法、人工智能（将它们视为某种人工智能单元），我们可以为自己的产品创造不同的体验，并且我们可以通过相同的平台技术将相同的技术移植到其他人的产品中。

blocks.html_en: What that’s creating is a lot of efficiency at the research and development level. It’s creating more breadth because now that we’re thinking about things like noise cancellation for different spaces, spatial audio, or hearing what you want, it is actually creating more innovation and more invention at the core. It’s making us faster because we’ve made these building blocks a lot more consumable for our B2B customers; it makes us faster at bringing our own products to market, too.

sentences.en: What that’s creating is a lot of efficiency at the research and development level.
sentences.zh: 这在研发层面创造了很高的效率。

sentences.en: It’s creating more breadth because now that we’re thinking about things like noise cancellation for different spaces, spatial audio, or hearing what you want, it is actually creating more innovation and more invention at the core.
sentences.zh: 它创造了更多的广度，因为现在我们正在考虑诸如不同空间的噪音消除、空间音频或听到您想要的声音之类的事情，它实际上正在创造更多的创新和更多的核心发明。

sentences.en: It’s making us faster because we’ve made these building blocks a lot more consumable for our B2B customers; it makes us faster at bringing our own products to market, too.
sentences.zh: 它使我们的速度更快，因为我们使这些构建块对于我们的 B2B 客户来说更容易使用；它也使我们能够更快地将自己的产品推向市场。

blocks.html_en: I think this is a great place to ask the Decoder questions because you’re describing the endpoint of a pretty big culture and structure shift at Bose that you’ve been architecting for several years. So how is Bose structured today?

sentences.en: I think this is a great place to ask the Decoder questions because you’re describing the endpoint of a pretty big culture and structure shift at Bose that you’ve been architecting for several years.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是询问 Decoder 问题的好地方，因为您正在描述 Bose 多年来一直在构建的相当大的文化和结构转变的终点。

sentences.en: So how is Bose structured today?
sentences.zh: 那么 Bose 如今的结构如何？

blocks.html_en: There’s a business unit structure, there’s a functional structure, and we are living in what I would describe as a hybrid. So for the core functions that matter deeply to what we deliver, like engineering, marketing, and supply chain, those are global functions that support all of our businesses. But because we’ve added new customer sets and really two new businesses with luxury and audio tech, we’re also running four business units. So those four business units have business unit presidents, and they draw on the global functions for the work that they need.

sentences.en: There’s a business unit structure, there’s a functional structure, and we are living in what I would describe as a hybrid.
sentences.zh: 有一个业务单元结构，有一个职能结构，我们生活在我所描述的混合体中。

sentences.en: So for the core functions that matter deeply to what we deliver, like engineering, marketing, and supply chain, those are global functions that support all of our businesses.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于与我们交付的产品密切相关的核心职能，如工程、营销和供应链，这些都是支持我们所有业务的全球职能。

sentences.en: But because we’ve added new customer sets and really two new businesses with luxury and audio tech, we’re also running four business units.
sentences.zh: 但由于我们增加了新的客户群以及两项涉及奢侈品和音频技术的新业务，因此我们还运营着四个业务部门。

sentences.en: So those four business units have business unit presidents, and they draw on the global functions for the work that they need.
sentences.zh: 因此，这四个业务部门都有业务部门总裁，他们利用全球职能来完成所需的工作。

blocks.html_en: How many people is Bose today?

sentences.en: How many people is Bose today?
sentences.zh: Bose 今天有多少人？

blocks.html_en: And you’re mostly in Framingham, or are you all over the place?

sentences.en: And you’re mostly in Framingham, or are you all over the place?
sentences.zh: 您大部分时间都在弗雷明汉，还是到处都是？

blocks.html_en: We’re global. All over. Yep.

sentences.en: We’re global.
sentences.zh: 我们是全球性的。

sentences.en: All over.
sentences.zh: 遍。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

blocks.html_en: You said you’re a hybrid. How’s that split between engineering, sales, all that sort of thing?

sentences.en: You said you’re a hybrid.
sentences.zh: 你说你是混血儿。

sentences.en: How’s that split between engineering, sales, all that sort of thing?
sentences.zh: 工程、销售等工作之间是如何划分的？

blocks.html_en: I don’t actually think about it that way, but the one thing that I do know — sort of the most important statistic to me — is that half of our employees are engineers.

sentences.en: I don’t actually think about it that way, but the one thing that I do know — sort of the most important statistic to me — is that half of our employees are engineers.
sentences.zh: 我实际上并不这么认为，但我确实知道的一件事——对我来说最重要的统计数据——是我们一半的员工是工程师。

blocks.html_en: You’re describing AWS, you’re describing Amazon. You’ve modularized a bunch of components inside the company; now you can build new products faster. This is really great. Every company that goes through this transition ends up hiring more and more engineers over time because you just need to build more and more components. Has that been growing? Are you investing more in that kind of engineering?

sentences.en: You’re describing AWS, you’re describing Amazon.
sentences.zh: 你在描述AWS，你在描述亚马逊。

sentences.en: You’ve modularized a bunch of components inside the company; now you can build new products faster.
sentences.zh: 你已经在公司内部模块化了一堆组件；现在您可以更快地构建新产品。

sentences.en: This is really great.
sentences.zh: 这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Every company that goes through this transition ends up hiring more and more engineers over time because you just need to build more and more components.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，每家经历这种转变的公司最终都会雇佣越来越多的工程师，因为你只需要构建越来越多的组件。

sentences.en: Has that been growing?
sentences.zh: 那一直在增长吗？

sentences.en: Are you investing more in that kind of engineering?
sentences.zh: 您是否会在此类工程上投入更多资金？

blocks.html_en: We are for sure. I think it’s probably not unique to us. We’ve been in this transition of hardware long, long ago. It was just hardware, and then hardware and software, and then more and more software. And now as we’re building the technology pieces, those are truly just software products that are an algorithm- or AI-based product that we’re selling with.

sentences.en: We are for sure.
sentences.zh: 我们确信。

sentences.en: I think it’s probably not unique to us.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能不是我们所独有的。

sentences.en: We’ve been in this transition of hardware long, long ago.
sentences.zh: 很久很久以前，我们就已经经历了硬件的转变。

sentences.en: It was just hardware, and then hardware and software, and then more and more software.
sentences.zh: 这只是硬件，然后是硬件和软件，然后是越来越多的软件。

sentences.en: And now as we’re building the technology pieces, those are truly just software products that are an algorithm- or AI-based product that we’re selling with.
sentences.zh: 现在，当我们构建技术部件时，这些实际上只是软件产品，是我们销售的基于算法或人工智能的产品。

blocks.html_en: You see that mixed shift continuing. We’re certainly seeing growth in our engineering ranks. And we’re getting a lot more productivity out of engineering as we start to have more sophisticated tools, as we use AI and other things to help with some of that development. So yes, growing. And I think more productivity per engineer, if you will, as we start to use more sophisticated tools to do the development.

sentences.en: You see that mixed shift continuing.
sentences.zh: 你会看到这种混合转变仍在继续。

sentences.en: We’re certainly seeing growth in our engineering ranks.
sentences.zh: 我们确实看到了我们的工程队伍的增长。

sentences.en: And we’re getting a lot more productivity out of engineering as we start to have more sophisticated tools, as we use AI and other things to help with some of that development.
sentences.zh: 随着我们开始拥有更复杂的工具，使用人工智能和其他东西来帮助进行一些开发，我们从工程中获得了更多的生产力。

sentences.en: So yes, growing.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，成长。

sentences.en: And I think more productivity per engineer, if you will, as we start to use more sophisticated tools to do the development.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，我认为每个工程师的生产力都会提高，因为我们开始使用更复杂的工具来进行开发。

blocks.html_en: You said it’s pure software products, right? When you sell out to B2B, you’re just selling the algorithms. Do those feel protectable? This is one of the things that I think about all the time. What is the actual thing you’re selling, and how easily can it be copied by a Chinese firm that does not respect our intellectual property laws or something like that?

sentences.en: You said it’s pure software products, right?
sentences.zh: 你说的是纯软件产品吧？

sentences.en: When you sell out to B2B, you’re just selling the algorithms.
sentences.zh: 当你向 B2B 出售产品时，你只是在出售算法。

sentences.en: Do those feel protectable?
sentences.zh: 那些感觉受到保护吗？

sentences.en: This is one of the things that I think about all the time.
sentences.zh: 这是我一直在思考的事情之一。

sentences.en: What is the actual thing you’re selling, and how easily can it be copied by a Chinese firm that does not respect our intellectual property laws or something like that?
sentences.zh: 你们销售的实际产品是什么？它有多容易被不尊重我们知识产权法或类似法律的中国公司复制？

blocks.html_en: Yeah. I’m probably oversimplifying. We’re really selling three things. We’re definitely selling software, algorithms, et cetera. I’ll come back to your “how do you protect it?” question. One of the very special things about Bose is actually systems engineering, which is an underappreciated discipline in my view. So software’s great, but software has to run on hardware in our world. Ultimately, that software has to get delivered through something.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I’m probably oversimplifying.
sentences.zh: 我可能过于简单化了。

sentences.en: We’re really selling three things.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上卖三样东西。

sentences.en: We’re definitely selling software, algorithms, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 我们肯定是在销售软件、算法等等。

sentences.en: I’ll come back to your “how do you protect it?”
sentences.zh: 我会回到你的“你如何保护它？”

sentences.en: question.
sentences.zh: 问题。

sentences.en: One of the very special things about Bose is actually systems engineering, which is an underappreciated discipline in my view.
sentences.zh: Bose 的一个非常特别的地方实际上是系统工程，在我看来，这是一个未被充分重视的学科。

sentences.en: So software’s great, but software has to run on hardware in our world.
sentences.zh: 所以软件很棒，但在我们的世界中，软件必须在硬件上运行。

sentences.en: Ultimately, that software has to get delivered through something.
sentences.zh: 最终，该软件必须通过某些东西来交付。

blocks.html_en: The magic at Bose, the secret sauce, has always been systems engineering and how you’re marrying together hardware and software elements for an experience that feels unified across the device and that’s optimized to provide the best experiences. So we’re certainly doing that on our own products, but you see that kind of a service as we start to sell more and more technology into our B2B customers.

sentences.en: The magic at Bose, the secret sauce, has always been systems engineering and how you’re marrying together hardware and software elements for an experience that feels unified across the device and that’s optimized to provide the best experiences.
sentences.zh: Bose 的魔力、秘密武器始终是系统工程，以及如何将硬件和软件元素结合在一起，以获得跨设备统一的体验，并经过优化以提供最佳体验。

sentences.en: So we’re certainly doing that on our own products, but you see that kind of a service as we start to sell more and more technology into our B2B customers.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们当然会在自己的产品上这样做，但是当我们开始向 B2B 客户销售越来越多的技术时，您会看到这种服务。

blocks.html_en: There’s also a lot of desire for help on that system side because our expertise there is real. That’s always been true in our automotive business, and it is increasingly true in our partnerships and our customers on the audio tech side as well. So I think that the second piece, which is really important to call out, is that it’s not just software for software’s sake. It’s software that has to be integrated into a system where everything comes together to work. And then you’ve got kind of the idea of systems engineering and then services on top of that.

sentences.en: There’s also a lot of desire for help on that system side because our expertise there is real.
sentences.zh: 在系统方面也有很多寻求帮助的愿望，因为我们在这方面的专业知识是真实的。

sentences.en: That’s always been true in our automotive business, and it is increasingly true in our partnerships and our customers on the audio tech side as well.
sentences.zh: 在我们的汽车业务中一直如此，在我们的合作伙伴和音频技术方面的客户中也越来越如此。

sentences.en: So I think that the second piece, which is really important to call out, is that it’s not just software for software’s sake.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为第二点非常重要，那就是它不仅仅是为了软件而软件。

sentences.en: It’s software that has to be integrated into a system where everything comes together to work.
sentences.zh: 它的软件必须集成到一个系统中，让所有东西都可以一起工作。

sentences.en: And then you’ve got kind of the idea of systems engineering and then services on top of that.
sentences.zh: 然后你就有了系统工程的想法，然后在此基础上提供服务。

blocks.html_en: So, how you tune a product. Some of our partners and customers need help with that, want help with that; some don’t. There are a lot of services that get married along. Sometimes it’s systems engineering. Sometimes it’s things like tuning, et cetera. So three pieces.

sentences.en: So, how you tune a product.
sentences.zh: 那么，如何调整产品。

sentences.en: Some of our partners and customers need help with that, want help with that; some don’t.
sentences.zh: 我们的一些合作伙伴和客户在这方面需要帮助，希望得到帮助；有些则不然。

sentences.en: There are a lot of services that get married along.
sentences.zh: 有很多与婚姻相关的服务。

sentences.en: Sometimes it’s systems engineering.
sentences.zh: 有时它是系统工程。

sentences.en: Sometimes it’s things like tuning, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 有时是诸如调整之类的事情。

sentences.en: So three pieces.
sentences.zh: 所以三块。

blocks.html_en: Can I play devil’s advocate here for one second? What you’re describing here, if you wanted to poke at it as hard as you could, is a process of a little bit of commodification. There are a lot of common components here, and then it’s the layers on top that differentiate in the market.

sentences.en: Can I play devil’s advocate here for one second?
sentences.zh: 我可以在这里唱反调吗？

sentences.en: What you’re describing here, if you wanted to poke at it as hard as you could, is a process of a little bit of commodification.
sentences.zh: 如果你想尽你所能地探究它，你在这里所描述的是一个有点商品化的过程。

sentences.en: There are a lot of common components here, and then it’s the layers on top that differentiate in the market.
sentences.zh: 这里有很多常见的组件，然后是顶层在市场上的差异化。

blocks.html_en: If you’re an audio nerd, the magazines are all saying one engineer in their garage innovated on speaker technology, and they made the speaker cones out of waffle paper, and now they’re more transparent than ever. Whatever that myth was that sold a lot of speakers back in the day.

sentences.en: If you’re an audio nerd, the magazines are all saying one engineer in their garage innovated on speaker technology, and they made the speaker cones out of waffle paper, and now they’re more transparent than ever.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个音频迷，杂志都说他们车库里的一位工程师在扬声器技术上进行了创新，他们用华夫纸制作了扬声器锥体，现在它们比以往任何时候都更加透明。

sentences.en: Whatever that myth was that sold a lot of speakers back in the day.
sentences.zh: 无论这个神话是什么，当时都卖出了很多扬声器。

blocks.html_en: If we’re not starting from the products back, but you’re starting from the components up, there’s a risk that everything kind of becomes the same, and it’s branding and marketing, and maybe the sound signature that’s tuned into it is artificial now — it’s not from the components themselves. How do you balance that? Or is that just not a worry with modern consumers?

sentences.en: If we’re not starting from the products back, but you’re starting from the components up, there’s a risk that everything kind of becomes the same, and it’s branding and marketing, and maybe the sound signature that’s tuned into it is artificial now — it’s not from the components themselves.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不是从产品开始，而是从组件开始，那么就有可能一切都变得相同，这是品牌和营销，也许现在调整到它的声音特征是人为的 - 它不是来自组件本身。

sentences.en: How do you balance that?
sentences.zh: 你如何平衡这一点？

sentences.en: Or is that just not a worry with modern consumers?
sentences.zh: 或者这对于现代消费者来说并不是一个令人担忧的问题？

blocks.html_en: I think what you’re describing is that if we’re putting Bose technology in other headphones, doesn’t that just revert to the mean? I think there’s a second, bigger market for us that is not audio products. Things that we call audio second. So for example, the XR glasses, the main function is not audio, but audio is really important. You don’t usually buy a car because it has a Bose sound system, but when you buy the car, the sound system is actually one of the most important features of the car.

sentences.en: I think what you’re describing is that if we’re putting Bose technology in other headphones, doesn’t that just revert to the mean?
sentences.zh: 我认为您所描述的是，如果我们将 Bose 技术应用到其他耳机中，那不是会回归到平均值吗？

sentences.en: I think there’s a second, bigger market for us that is not audio products.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们还有第二个更大的市场，它不是音频产品。

sentences.en: Things that we call audio second.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为音频第二的东西。

sentences.en: So for example, the XR glasses, the main function is not audio, but audio is really important.
sentences.zh: 所以比如说XR眼镜，主要功能不是音频，但是音频确实很重要。

sentences.en: You don’t usually buy a car because it has a Bose sound system, but when you buy the car, the sound system is actually one of the most important features of the car.
sentences.zh: 你通常不会因为有 Bose 音响系统而买车，但当你买车时，音响系统实际上是汽车最重要的功能之一。

blocks.html_en: A projector that you buy for your house, you’re buying because it’s a great projector. We’re partnering with Epson, and the sound is also really important there. So it’s a little bit different, I think, when you get into audio second. In the audio market, I think that the key is that there are so many different customers who want different things.

sentences.en: A projector that you buy for your house, you’re buying because it’s a great projector.
sentences.zh: 您为自己的房子购买一台投影仪，您购买它是因为它是一台很棒的投影仪。

sentences.en: We’re partnering with Epson, and the sound is also really important there.
sentences.zh: 我们正在与爱普生合作，声音也非常重要。

sentences.en: So it’s a little bit different, I think, when you get into audio second.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，当你进入音频第二阶段时，情况有点不同。

sentences.en: In the audio market, I think that the key is that there are so many different customers who want different things.
sentences.zh: 在音频市场，我认为关键是有很多不同的客户想要不同的东西。

blocks.html_en: When you think about products that have ingredient technology that’s the same, it’s really enabling you to do things for your customer and the experience that you’re trying to create. I’ll just use Skullcandy as an example. Skullcandy just launched a pair of headphones with Sound by Bose, and you couldn’t have two more diverse customer sets between who they’re targeting and who we’re targeting. We helped them with the technology. So there’s Bose technology inside to help make that sound better, but the design choices of what they want for their customer are incredibly different from what you would find [with Bose].

sentences.en: When you think about products that have ingredient technology that’s the same, it’s really enabling you to do things for your customer and the experience that you’re trying to create.
sentences.zh: 当您想到具有相同成分技术的产品时，它确实使您能够为您的客户做事并创造您想要创造的体验。

sentences.en: I’ll just use Skullcandy as an example.
sentences.zh: 我仅以 Skullcandy 为例。

sentences.en: Skullcandy just launched a pair of headphones with Sound by Bose, and you couldn’t have two more diverse customer sets between who they’re targeting and who we’re targeting.
sentences.zh: Skullcandy 刚刚推出了一款配备 Sound by Bose 的耳机，他们的目标客户和我们的目标客户之间不可能有两个更加多样化的客户群。

sentences.en: We helped them with the technology.
sentences.zh: 我们用技术帮助他们。

sentences.en: So there’s Bose technology inside to help make that sound better, but the design choices of what they want for their customer are incredibly different from what you would find [with Bose].
sentences.zh: 因此，内部的 Bose 技术可帮助改善音质，但他们为客户提供的设计选择与您在 [Bose] 中发现的设计选择截然不同。

blocks.html_en: So I don’t think you would ever put those two products, a Bose headphone and a Skullcandy headphone, side by side and say, “Wow, this is really commoditized. It sounds the same. It is the same.” They’re very, very, very different.

sentences.en: So I don’t think you would ever put those two products, a Bose headphone and a Skullcandy headphone, side by side and say, “Wow, this is really commoditized.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为您不会将 Bose 耳机和 Skullcandy 耳机这两种产品并排放置并说：“哇，这真的是商品化了。

sentences.en: It sounds the same.
sentences.zh: 听起来是一样的。

sentences.en: It is the same.”
sentences.zh: 是一样的。”

sentences.en: They’re very, very, very different.
sentences.zh: 他们非常非常不同。

blocks.html_en: I think I’m asking slightly more about the audio-second product. If all of your audio-first products come from the same technology base, the same modular components that can be remixed into all the products you want, do you lose the ability to innovate at the product level? If everything is made out of the same Legos, at some point you can’t be like, “Actually what I need is all new Legos.”

sentences.en: I think I’m asking slightly more about the audio-second product.
sentences.zh: 我想我对音频第二产品的询问稍微多一些。

sentences.en: If all of your audio-first products come from the same technology base, the same modular components that can be remixed into all the products you want, do you lose the ability to innovate at the product level?
sentences.zh: 如果您所有的音频优先产品都来自相同的技术基础，相同的模块化组件可以重新混合到您想要的所有产品中，您是否会失去产品级别的创新能力？

sentences.en: If everything is made out of the same Legos, at some point you can’t be like, “Actually what I need is all new Legos.”
sentences.zh: 如果所有东西都是用相同的乐高积木制成的，那么在某些时候你就不能说，“实际上我需要的是所有新的乐高积木。”

blocks.html_en: I think the answer is no, because the product is so much bigger than just those ingredients. So if you think about headphone design, the comfort and all of the other features, right? There may be a lot of ingredient technology, but the ones that you choose may be different.

sentences.en: I think the answer is no, because the product is so much bigger than just those ingredients.
sentences.zh: 我认为答案是否定的，因为产品比这些成分要大得多。

sentences.en: So if you think about headphone design, the comfort and all of the other features, right?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果您考虑耳机设计、舒适度和所有其他功能，对吧？

sentences.en: There may be a lot of ingredient technology, but the ones that you choose may be different.
sentences.zh: 成分技术可能有很多，但你选择的可能会有所不同。

blocks.html_en: One of the things that we talk a lot about now is being at the intelligent edge. Everything Bose does is what we would describe as at the intelligent edge. And as you know, it’s a pretty hostile environment. You have limited compute, you have limited power. You’re always making trade-offs between what I am putting in this product and how does that impact my ability to do that? Because there’s just not enough room to put everything in it.

sentences.en: One of the things that we talk a lot about now is being at the intelligent edge.
sentences.zh: 我们现在经常谈论的事情之一就是处于智能边缘。

sentences.en: Everything Bose does is what we would describe as at the intelligent edge.
sentences.zh: Bose 所做的一切都是我们所说的智能边缘。

sentences.en: And as you know, it’s a pretty hostile environment.
sentences.zh: 如您所知，这是一个非常敌对的环境。

sentences.en: You have limited compute, you have limited power.
sentences.zh: 你的计算能力有限，你的能力也有限。

sentences.en: You’re always making trade-offs between what I am putting in this product and how does that impact my ability to do that?
sentences.zh: 您总是在我在该产品中添加的内容以及这对我的能力有何影响之间进行权衡？

sentences.en: Because there’s just not enough room to put everything in it.
sentences.zh: 因为没有足够的空间来放置所有东西。

blocks.html_en: So I think the reason why you still see so much differentiation among products, even if some of the ingredients are the same, is because all of those product choices that you’re making are really critical, and you have to make a lot of them to fit inside that constrained environment that you’re working with.

sentences.en: So I think the reason why you still see so much differentiation among products, even if some of the ingredients are the same, is because all of those product choices that you’re making are really critical, and you have to make a lot of them to fit inside that constrained environment that you’re working with.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为即使某些成分相同，您仍然看到产品之间存在如此大的差异，是因为您所做的所有这些产品选择都非常关键，并且您必须制造大量产品以适应您正在使用的受限环境。

blocks.html_en: This brings me to the other Decoder question about decisions. You’ve obviously made a lot of them, and you’ve got a few big ones to make that I want to come to concerning AI. How do you make decisions? What’s your framework?

sentences.en: This brings me to the other Decoder question about decisions.
sentences.zh: 这让我想到了解码器的另一个关于决策的问题。

sentences.en: You’ve obviously made a lot of them, and you’ve got a few big ones to make that I want to come to concerning AI.
sentences.zh: 显然你们已经做了很多这样的事情，而且还有一些我想谈谈人工智能的大事情要做。

sentences.en: How do you make decisions?
sentences.zh: 你如何做决定？

sentences.en: What’s your framework?
sentences.zh: 你的框架是什么？

blocks.html_en: I am a believer that you get the right people in the room, you have an intense debate that isn’t always comfortable, that sometimes makes people a little bit queasy, and you move as fast as you can to decide, knowing that if it’s wrong, you can pivot. That is, in my simplest terms, the way I think about it.

sentences.en: I am a believer that you get the right people in the room, you have an intense debate that isn’t always comfortable, that sometimes makes people a little bit queasy, and you move as fast as you can to decide, knowing that if it’s wrong, you can pivot.
sentences.zh: 我相信房间里有合适的人，你会进行激烈的辩论，但这种辩论并不总是让人舒服，有时会让人们有点不安，你会尽快做出决定，知道如果错了，你可以改变方向。

sentences.en: That is, in my simplest terms, the way I think about it.
sentences.zh: 用我最简单的话来说，这就是我的思考方式。

blocks.html_en: We get a lot of type one and type two decisions, move fast, in that we had an ex-Amazon employee write to us and say, “Every decision is reversible if you have enough money.”

sentences.en: We get a lot of type one and type two decisions, move fast, in that we had an ex-Amazon employee write to us and say, “Every decision is reversible if you have enough money.”
sentences.zh: 我们得到了很多第一类和第二类决策，行动迅速，因为我们有一位前亚马逊员工写信给我们说：“如果你有足够的钱，每个决定都是可逆的。”

blocks.html_en: [Laughs] That might be true for Amazon.

sentences.en: [Laughs] That might be true for Amazon.
sentences.zh: [笑]对于亚马逊来说可能是这样。

blocks.html_en: That’s a very Amazon perspective. The reason I bring this up in the context of AI is that I’m looking at the sweep of things you’re doing, and I’m looking at where, in particular, the big tech companies think their headphones are going to go.

sentences.en: That’s a very Amazon perspective.

sentences.en: The reason I bring this up in the context of AI is that I’m looking at the sweep of things you’re doing, and I’m looking at where, in particular, the big tech companies think their headphones are going to go.
sentences.zh: 我在人工智能的背景下提出这个问题的原因是，我正在研究你正在做的事情，特别是大型科技公司认为他们的耳机将走向何方。

blocks.html_en: I was reviewing our conversation from four years ago. Boy, did we talk about Bluetooth a lot. We did. This is a core limiting technology. And then their products, their first-party products, get to extend that standard in different ways — and they all do it.

sentences.en: I was reviewing our conversation from four years ago.
sentences.zh: 我正在回顾我们四年前的谈话。

sentences.en: Boy, did we talk about Bluetooth a lot.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我们谈论蓝牙很多了吗？

sentences.en: We did.
sentences.zh: 我们做到了。

sentences.en: This is a core limiting technology.
sentences.zh: 这是一个核心限制技术。

sentences.en: It’s an enabling technology in an important way, but they hold onto what Bluetooth can and can’t do on their platforms very tightly.
sentences.zh: 这是一种重要的支持技术，但他们非常严格地控制着蓝牙在其平台上能做什么和不能做什么。

sentences.en: And then their products, their first-party products, get to extend that standard in different ways — and they all do it.
sentences.zh: 然后他们的产品，他们的第一方产品，以不同的方式扩展该标准 - 他们都这样做了。

blocks.html_en: This broadly means if you have an iPhone, the best working headphones that will do all the things the platform wants you to do are probably AirPods. If you have a Pixel, it’s probably Pixel Buds. If you have a Samsung phone, it’s probably their buds.

sentences.en: This broadly means if you have an iPhone, the best working headphones that will do all the things the platform wants you to do are probably AirPods.
sentences.zh: 这大致意味着，如果您有 iPhone，那么能够完成该平台希望您做的所有事情的最佳工作耳机可能是 AirPods。

blocks.html_en: And this is because they have reduced the capability of the interconnect. sentences.en: And this is because they have reduced the capability of the interconnect.
sentences.zh: 这是因为它们降低了互连的能力。

sentences.en: One of the reasons they’re doing that is because they want your earbuds in your ears 24/7 so you can talk to their AI systems on the back end.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做的原因之一是因为他们希望你的耳塞 24/7 都在你的耳朵里，这样你就可以在后端与他们的人工智能系统交谈。

sentences.en: And this is their future.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的未来。

sentences.zh: 也许答案是我们都会佩戴 Meta Glasses，或者我们都会佩戴 Xreal 眼镜。

sentences.zh: 您认为这里还有第三方玩家的空间吗？

blocks.html_en: We absolutely think wearables are critical to the AI future. I think that we’re clear on that. The form factor, if you work backwards from that, we’re going to use our wearable devices to communicate with our AI agents. And that is going to become more and more important and more and more natural. We strongly believe that.

sentences.en: We absolutely think wearables are critical to the AI future.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对认为可穿戴设备对人工智能的未来至关重要。

sentences.en: I think that we’re clear on that.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们对此很清楚。

sentences.en: The form factor, if you work backwards from that, we’re going to use our wearable devices to communicate with our AI agents.
sentences.zh: 外形因素，如果你从这个角度倒推，我们将使用我们的可穿戴设备与我们的人工智能代理进行通信。

sentences.en: And that is going to become more and more important and more and more natural.
sentences.zh: 这将变得越来越重要、越来越自然。

sentences.en: We strongly believe that.
sentences.zh: 我们坚信这一点。

blocks.html_en: The second thing we believe is that it is more likely to be conversational and sound-based than anything else. At least we think that is probably the primary mode. And so the types of technologies we’re focused on are around voice pickup, clarity, speech enablement, and we think all are incredibly important. What form factor you want to use as your wearable, I think the jury is still out. I think the answer is going to be a whole proliferation of them. Some people will like glasses because they like the glasses.

sentences.en: The second thing we believe is that it is more likely to be conversational and sound-based than anything else.
sentences.zh: 我们相信的第二件事是，它比其他任何东西都更有可能是对话性的和基于声音的。

sentences.en: At least we think that is probably the primary mode.
sentences.zh: 至少我们认为这可能是主要模式。

sentences.en: And so the types of technologies we’re focused on are around voice pickup, clarity, speech enablement, and we think all are incredibly important.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们关注的技术类型是围绕语音拾取、清晰度、语音支持，我们认为所有这些都非常重要。

sentences.en: What form factor you want to use as your wearable, I think the jury is still out.
sentences.zh: 你想使用什么外形尺寸作为你的可穿戴设备，我认为目前还没有定论。

sentences.en: I think the answer is going to be a whole proliferation of them.
sentences.zh: 我认为答案将是它们的全面扩散。

sentences.en: Some people will like glasses because they like the glasses.
sentences.zh: 有些人会喜欢眼镜，因为他们喜欢眼镜。

blocks.html_en: Some people will like open earbuds, which we hadn’t launched when you and I talked last time. sentences.en: Some people will like open earbuds, which we hadn’t launched when you and I talked last time.

sentences.en: We talked a lot about open ear audio, but not yet about that form factor, that clip-on form factor that Bose invented and launched into the world.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论了很多关于开放式耳机的音频，但还没有讨论 Bose 发明并向世界推出的夹式外形。

sentences.en: We think that is a really powerful form factor that will be for some.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这对某些人来说是一个非常强大的外形因素。

sentences.en: Others might want a watch, a pin, a ring, or 18 variations of how those work together.
sentences.zh: 其他人可能想要一块手表、一枚别针、一枚戒指，或者这些物品的 18 种组合方式。

blocks.html_en: Part of the reason we think being in the audio tech business is important is that it gives us the ability to participate in a lot of those different places that we might not naturally be able to go on our own. So we think form factor is going to matter, but I don’t think there’s a single winner there. At least that’s my current view. I think that there will be multiple types of devices that consumers will choose based on their own personal preferences.

sentences.en: Part of the reason we think being in the audio tech business is important is that it gives us the ability to participate in a lot of those different places that we might not naturally be able to go on our own.
sentences.zh: 我们认为进入音频技术行业很重要，部分原因是它使我们有能力参与许多不同的领域，而我们自然无法独自去往这些领域。

sentences.en: So we think form factor is going to matter, but I don’t think there’s a single winner there.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们认为外形因素很重要，但我认为没有一个赢家。

sentences.en: At least that’s my current view.
sentences.zh: 至少这是我目前的观点。

sentences.en: I think that there will be multiple types of devices that consumers will choose based on their own personal preferences.
sentences.zh: 我认为将会有多种类型的设备，消费者会根据自己的个人喜好进行选择。

blocks.html_en: We know there are going to be a limited number of LLMs, right? We know that those are going to converge to the large ecosystems that already exist. New ones may emerge, as we’re seeing, but there won’t be hundreds of those. There will be few of those. And yes, there may be some advantages if you stay within that ecosystem for your earbuds. But fundamentally, I think even though a lot of people choose earbuds, headphones, and other devices in their ecosystem, a lot of people don’t.

sentences.en: We know there are going to be a limited number of LLMs, right?
sentences.zh: 我们知道法学硕士的数量有限，对吗？

sentences.en: We know that those are going to converge to the large ecosystems that already exist.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这些将汇聚到已经存在的大型生态系统中。

sentences.en: New ones may emerge, as we’re seeing, but there won’t be hundreds of those.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所看到的，新的可能会出现，但不会有数百个。

sentences.en: There will be few of those.
sentences.zh: 其中很少有。

sentences.zh: 是的，如果你的耳机留在这个生态系统中，可能会有一些优势。

sentences.en: But fundamentally, I think even though a lot of people choose earbuds, headphones, and other devices in their ecosystem, a lot of people don’t.
sentences.zh: 但从根本上说，我认为即使很多人在他们的生态系统中选择耳塞、耳机和其他设备，但也有很多人没有这样做。

blocks.html_en: I think consumers still want choice. And I think it is important for those ecosystems. In our conversations with them, they need third-party players to interface with their AI as well. sentences.en: I think consumers still want choice.
sentences.zh: 我认为消费者仍然需要选择。

sentences.en: And I think it is important for those ecosystems.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对于这些生态系统很重要。

sentences.en: In our conversations with them, they need third-party players to interface with their AI as well.

sentences.en: They need third-party players to produce devices that work with what they’re doing because they recognize that they’re not going to have a full share of the market and that choice matters.

blocks.html_en: So we believe we’ve got a couple of ways to compete now. Our own devices, for sure, need to be compatible across the different LLMs and the ability to interface with them. And we need our technology starting to crop up in other places where that interface will happen.

sentences.en: So we believe we’ve got a couple of ways to compete now.
sentences.zh: 所以我们相信我们现在有几种竞争方式。

sentences.en: Our own devices, for sure, need to be compatible across the different LLMs and the ability to interface with them.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们自己的设备需要跨不同的法学硕士兼容并能够与它们交互。

sentences.en: And we need our technology starting to crop up in other places where that interface will happen.
sentences.zh: 我们需要我们的技术开始出现在其他将出现该界面的地方。

blocks.html_en: Is this a way to just hedge the bet that no one actually knows what’s going to happen with AI? sentences.en: There’s certainly a diversification play, absolutely.

sentences.zh: Bose 的品牌宗旨是：我们为音乐爱好者服务。

blocks.html_en: One of the things I worry about, again, as a music fan, as an audio nerd, is every single time the tech companies come to music, convenience wins, and quality suffers. blocks.html_en: When it comes to adding AI, we talk about it at Bose as tiny AI. A lot of companies are good at really big AI.
